summary: RFC 5785 defines the /.well-known/ path prefix for http and https. This memo formally updates RFC 6455 so the same well-known URI mechanism can also be used with the ws and wss URI schemes of the WebSocket Protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: Well-known URIs provide standard paths for finding information about a service. This RFC formally lets WebSocket addresses using ws or wss use that mechanism and its existing registry.

questions: are well-known uris available for ws and wss
do ws and wss share the well-known uri registry
subtitle: The /.well-known/ URI mechanism formally applies to ws and wss schemes.

tldr.problem: RFC 5785 defined well-known URIs for http and https, while RFC 6455 did not define them for the WebSocket schemes ws and wss.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC updates RFC 6455 so ws and wss use the same well-known URI suffix registry established by RFC 5785.
tldr.outcome: No IANA action is needed; applications defining WebSocket-specific suffixes should consider information exposure through the equivalent HTTP(S) URI.

today: RFC 8307 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6455. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Well-Known URIs for WebSocket
sections.content:
RFC 5785 defines the /.well-known path prefix and a registry of URI suffixes. It specifically covered http and https; other schemes later used the mechanism and shared its registry.

RFC 6455 defines the ws and wss schemes but did not specify well-known URIs for them. This RFC formally extends the mechanism to those schemes.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 6455 defines the ws and wss WebSocket address schemes. This update lets them use the well-known URI path and the existing suffix registry.

sections.title: The Existing URI Registry
sections.content: Well-known URIs for ws and wss share the URI suffix registry established by RFC 5785. The update requires no registry changes and no IANA action.
sections.plainLanguage: WebSocket uses the existing list of well-known URI suffixes. No new registry entry is needed.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 5785 apply to all well-known URIs. The RFC says it creates no new security considerations by formally enabling the mechanism for ws and wss.

Applications defining suffixes specifically for WebSocket use should consider whether resources at the equivalent HTTP(S) URI could disclose information or create other security concerns.
sections.plainLanguage: Applications should check what information is available at the matching HTTP or HTTPS address. A WebSocket-specific path could expose the same resource there.

references.text: Nottingham, M. and E. Hammer-Lahav, "Defining Well-Known Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs)", RFC 5785, April 2010.
Fette, I. and A. Melnikov, "The WebSocket Protocol", RFC 6455, December 2011.
